name: Buffy Citrine
lede: Buffy Citrine is a dull gold-brown named for citrine, the yellow gem, and recorded by Ridgway in 1912 under the Japanese name Yanagicha, or willow tea.

sections.title: A gem's name, with a Japanese twin
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[rustic-drab]], [[metallic-sunburst]], [[dusty-hazel-tone]] and [[dull-citrine]], at 3, 4.4, 4.4 and 4.7 ΔE [1]. The same library entry carries the Japanese name Yanagicha, written 柳茶 and meaning willow tea [1].

A near-duplicate swatch in our data, Olive Lake, sits only 2.2 units off under a different name [1]. A second library color, [[citrine-drab]], is built on the same gem word but reads paler and greyer [1]. In LCH terms Buffy Citrine is mid-toned and moderately chromatic: lightness 55, chroma 34, hue 90 degrees [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Buffy Citrine in 2,417, about 10.2 percent, as photographed [2]. It covers most of the frame in Chinese and Japanese works, including an undated bird-and-branch painting and John Singer Sargent's *Study of Two Bedouins* of 1905, where it fills about 77 percent of the canvas [2]. Its heaviest use, relative to each painter's own baseline, falls to Paulus Potter, Johan Hendrik Weissenbruch and Mariano Fortuny Marsal, and the archive's use of it peaks in paintings from around 1400 [2].
